newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks surge to another record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks surge to another record close.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.935 +0.050 Gold NY 341.75 Lon fix 341.60
AUD US$0.7480 (Wed $0.7509) CRB Index cl 241.85 -3.04
*Stocks surge back from soft start to set record closing high as BHP and banks lead charge. Volume 409.40 million, value A$883.1 million, 1,202 traded, 315 steady, 407 up, 480 down
Australian stocks recovered after limping through early trade on Thursday to reach full stride late in the day and breast the tape for their fifth record close in a week.
The All Ordinaries Index dropped immediately after opening but was later spurred on by banks and leading miner BHP to close 19.9 points up at 2,693.3.
The June share price index futures contract also finished full of running to be up 16 points on 2,700.0 at the close.
"It was a weird sort of day, it started soft and surged at the end," said broker Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities.

The All Ordinaries was toying with the 2,700 mark at the same time as a Reuters poll was released showing some analysts said they expected the indicator to reach 2,720 by the end of December 1997 and push towards 3,000 over the next 18 months.
"It can get to 2,700, but not today," Cameron said.
Brokers and dealers agreed BHP was one of the star performers as shares in Australia's biggest listed company picked up 45 cents to close at A$19.72 on volume of 5.8 million.
BHP surged after analysts said they had revised up their profit forecasts for the embattled blue chip which this week announced a strong rise in copper production.
"BHP is very solid," said Cameron, who added overseas buying had helped push the All Ordinaries almost 12 points higher than the previous record set on Tuesday.

The banking sector also contributed to the rise in the All Ordinaries, which had dropped sharply immediately after opening in the wake of a third successive dip on Wall Street and a slump in gold price.
The banks index jumped 1.35 percent to break through the 4,800 barrier and finish on 4,829.2.
All four major banks closed over 12 cents or more higher, ANZ up 25 cents to A$9.80 on 1.6 million shares traded.

National Australia Bank jumped 18 cents to A$18.83 on trade of 1.2 million shares, Commonwealth Bank was up 15 cents at A$15.20 and Westpac rose 12 cents to A$7.87 after 2.8 million shares were traded.
"I think it's still people chasing yields and there's a bit of tax positioning as well," Cameron said.

Gold miner Normandy Mining NL was among the leaders in volume terms with 13.7 million shares changing hands, 12 million of them in the morning session. Normandy's share price ended one cent down on A$1.61.

Nickel producer QNI Ltd had a mixed first day back on the bourse since Wednesday's announcement of its merger with South Africa's Gencor Ltd, with brokers saying investors had still not digested all the details of the merger.
QNI shares ended three cents down from their level when trade was suspended on Tuesday pending the Gencor announcement.
Shares in Australia's second largest nickel producer started well but finished at A$2.65 on volume of 9.2 million shares.
Some brokers were surprised the shares did not trade higher, while others suggested institutional investors had decided the deal appeared more favourable to Gencor than QNI.
Shares in medical instrument designer Polartechnics Ltd soared after it announced an alliance with U.S. pharmaceutical group Johnson & Johnson to commercialise its cancer detection device.
Polartechnics shares rose 52 cents to close at A$3.00.
In other market news, Australian bond yields fell to 7.05 percent at the end of a drab day of trading with the benchmark 10 year T-bond up 0.045 points to 92.930.
The Australian dollar also had a listless day after tentative attempts at a recovery were hammered offshore and was stuck at US$0.7475/80 at 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT).
